comparison: Both address the central finding that k1 is only ~3 times faster than k3 (C3, C4, C24, C25, C47, C49, C50). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED by experimental data, while peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY about the nucleosome-based methodology used to separate these rates, questioning whether DNA fluctuations are truly faster than translocation for the 601 sequence near the dyad.

Perfect claim overlap (C9-C12) on velocity fitting to Michaelis-Menten kinetics. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval validates the methodology and parameter extraction, while peer reviewers acknowledge high data quality and do not challenge these foundational measurements.

Perfect claim overlap (C32-C35) on mutant's differential effects on short vs. long pauses. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. These observations are based on direct statistical comparisons on bare DNA, independent of the nucleosome methodology that reviewers question elsewhere.

OpenEval addresses broader nucleosome effects (C15-C23) finding them SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers focus specifically on the critical assumption about DNA fluctuation rates (C17-C19, C23) and express UNCERTAINTY, requesting direct evidence for wrapping/unwrapping kinetics near the 601 dyad.
